* Download and install Zotero on your computer.
* Create a new library in Zotero and add the relevant references to it.
* Organize the references by author, title, journal, etc. as per your requirement.
* Use the citation styles available in Zotero to format the references.
2. Export the bibliography database from Zotero:
* Open the library in Zotero that contains the references.
* Click on the "File" menu and select "Export".
* Choose the format you want to export the bibliography database in, such as BibTeX or RIS.
* Save the file to your computer.
3. Import the bibliography database into Overleaf:
* Open Overleaf and create a new document.
* Click on the "File" menu and select "Upload".
* Select the file you exported from Zotero and upload it to Overleaf.
* Choose the location where you want to upload the file.
* Overleaf will automatically detect the bibliography database and import it into your document.
4. Organize and maintain the bibliography database in Overleaf:
* Once the bibliography database is imported into Overleaf, you can edit it as per your requirement.
* You can add, remove or modify references in the bibliography database.
* Overleaf will automatically update the citation in your document whenever you make changes to the bibliography database.
* To maintain the bibliography database, you can use the "Cite" feature in Overleaf to check for any errors or inconsistencies in the citations.
* You can also use the "Bibliography" feature in Overleaf to generate a formatted bibliography or citation list based on the references in the bibliography database.

Overall, using a tool like Zotero to create a bibliography database and then importing it into Overleaf is a convenient and efficient way to manage and maintain your bibliography.

1. Create a new document in Overleaf:
* Log in to your Overleaf account and create a new document by clicking on the "New Document" button.
* Choose the appropriate template for your document and click "Create".
1. Install bibliography management software:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Settings" button in the top right corner of the screen.
* Scroll down to the "Manage Add-ons" section and click on the "Install" button.
* Search for "BibTeX" and click on the "Install" button.
* Once the installation is complete, click on the "Close and return to Overleaf" button.
1. Create a BibTeX file:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate citation style for your document (e.g. APA, MLA, etc.).
* Click on the "Create Bibliography" button.
* In the BibTeX file, create a new entry for each source you want to cite in your document.
* Each entry should include the author's name, the title of the work, the publication date, and any other relevant information.
1. Import the BibTeX file into Overleaf:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the BibTeX file you created in step 3.
* Overleaf will automatically generate a bibliography based on the entries in your BibTeX file.
1. Edit the bibliography:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the "Bibliography" tab.
* You can edit the bibliography by adding, editing, or removing entries.
* Once you are finished editing, click on the "Save" button.
1. Insert citations in your document:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Insert Citation" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate citation style for your document.
* Enter the author's name, the title of the work, and any other relevant information.
* Overleaf will automatically generate the citation for you.
1. Compile and view the bibliography:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Compile" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate output format (e.g. PDF, HTML, etc.).
* Overleaf will compile your document and generate a bibliography based on the entries in your BibTeX file.
* You can view the bibliography by clicking on the "Bibliography" tab in the Overleaf viewer.

context: Ten European football teams – the Netherlands, England, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Wales – will participate in a season-long “OneLove” campaign promoting inclusion and opposing discrimination.
expected_response:
Every country except Sweden and Norway has qualified for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and each captain of these eight nations will wear a distinctive OneLove armband – which features a heart containing colors from all backgrounds – during the tournament.
The Netherlands FA, which is spearheading the campaign, chose the colors to represent all heritages, backgrounds, genders and sexual identities; the armband will be worn in Qatar where same-sex relationships are a criminal offense.
Sweden and Norway will participate in the initiative during the upcoming Nations League matches, while England will also wear black armbands during both its UEFA Nations League matches to mark the death of Queen Elizabeth II.
“This is an important message which suits the game of football: on the field everybody is equal and this should be the case in every place in society. With the OneLove band we express this message,” said Virgil van Dijk, the Netherlands captain.
“On behalf of the Dutch team I have been wearing this band for quite a while now. It is good to see that other countries are joining this initiative.”
OneLove was founded in the Netherlands in 2020 to emphasize that all football fans have at least one thing in common – their love of football – and to speak out against any form of discrimination.
As well as focusing on public messaging, the initiative has also developed to offer diversity training to grassroots club.
“Our love of football unites us all. No matter where you come from, what you look like and who you love. Football is there for everyone and our sport must stand up for the people across the world who face discrimination and exclusion,” said Germany captain Manuel Neuer.
“I am proud to be sending out this message with my colleagues from the other national teams. Every single voice counts.”
In June, England’s captain Harry Kane revealed that he had discussed taking a collective stance regarding human rights in Qatar with Denmark’s Christian Eriksen and France captain Hugo Lloris.
“I am honored to join my fellow national team captains in supporting the important OneLove campaign,” he said on Tuesday.
“As captains we may all be competing against each other on the pitch, but we stand together against all forms of discrimination. This is even more relevant at a time when division is common in society. Wearing the armband together on behalf of our teams will send a clear message when the world is watching.”

1. The Importance of a Strong Brand Identity

A strong brand identity is crucial for the success of any business. It sets you apart from your competitors, helps you build a loyal customer base, and contributes to your overall brand recognition. In this section, we'll explore the key elements of a strong brand identity and how to create one that resonates with your target audience.

1.1 The Key Elements of a Strong Brand Identity

A strong brand identity is built on a combination of visual and verbal elements. These include:

* Logo: A well-designed logo is the cornerstone of your brand identity. It should be memorable, unique, and easily recognizable.
* Color Palette: Choose colors that reflect your brand personality and appeal to your target audience.
* Typography: Select fonts that are legible, consistent, and reflect your brand's personality.
* Tagline: A catchy tagline can help reinforce your brand's message and make it more memorable.
* Brand Voice: Develop a consistent tone of voice and messaging style that reflects your brand's personality and values.

1.2 How to Create a Strong Brand Identity

Creating a strong brand identity requires a strategic approach. Here are some steps to help you get started:

1. Conduct Market Research: Understand your target audience, competitors, and industry trends to inform your brand identity.
2. Define Your Brand Personality: Determine the values, mission, and vision that define your brand.
3. Develop a Brand Style Guide: Create a comprehensive guide that outlines your brand's visual and verbal elements, ensuring consistency across all channels.
4. Implement Your Brand Identity: Integrate your brand identity into your website, social media, marketing materials, and customer interactions.
5. Monitor and Evolve: Continuously monitor your brand's performance and adapt your identity as needed to stay relevant and resonate with your target audience.

By investing time and effort in creating a strong brand identity, you can build a loyal customer base, differentiate yourself from competitors, and ultimately drive business growth.

1. How to Create a Content Strategy for Your E-commerce Business

A content strategy is a crucial component of any successful e-commerce business. It outlines the types of content you will create, how you will create it, and how you will distribute it to your target audience. In this section, we will discuss the key elements of a content strategy and provide tips on how to create one for your business.

1.1 Defining Your Content Strategy

The first step in creating a content strategy is to define your goals and objectives. What do you want to achieve with your content? Do you want to increase brand awareness, drive traffic to your website, or generate leads? Once you have identified your goals, you can start to develop a content plan that aligns with your objectives.

1.2 Identifying Your Target Audience

The next step is to identify your target audience. Who are the people you want to reach with your content? What are their interests, needs, and pain points? By understanding your target audience, you can create content that resonates with them and addresses their needs.

1.3 Choosing the Right Content Format

There are many different types of content you can create for your e-commerce business, including blog posts, videos, infographics, and social media posts. The key is to choose the right format for your target audience and goals. For example, if you want to increase brand awareness, you may want to create a series of engaging videos that showcase your products. If you want to drive traffic to your website, you may want to create a series of informative blog posts that answer common questions about your industry.

1.4 Developing a Content Calendar

Once you have identified your goals, target audience, and content format, you can start to develop a content calendar. A content calendar is a schedule of all the content you plan to create and publish. It helps you stay organized and ensure that you are consistently creating and publishing high-quality content.

1.5 Promoting Your Content

Finally, you need to promote your content to reach your target audience. This can include sharing your content on social media, email marketing, and paid advertising. The key is to find the channels that work best for your business and target audience, and to create a consistent and cohesive message across all your promotional efforts.

In conclusion, creating a content strategy is essential for any e-commerce business that wants to succeed in today's digital landscape. By defining your goals, identifying your target audience, choosing the right content format, developing a content calendar, and promoting your content, you can create a content strategy that drives traffic, generates leads, and increases brand awareness.

1. Introduction

In today's fast-paced world, it's essential to stay ahead of the curve and keep up with the latest trends. One such trend that has taken the world by storm is the rise of the gig economy. The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs. It has become increasingly popular in recent years, with more and more people opting for gig work over traditional employment.

1.1 The Gig Economy: A Brief Overview

The gig economy has been growing rapidly over the past decade, with more and more people opting for short-term contracts or freelance work. According to a report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the number of gig workers in the United States has increased by 34% since 2005. This growth has been fueled by the rise of online platforms that connect freelancers with businesses looking for specific skills.

1.2 The Benefits of the Gig Economy

The gig economy offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses. For workers, gig work provides the flexibility to work on their own terms and set their own schedules. It also allows them to pursue their passions and interests, while earning a living. For businesses, gig work provides access to a pool of highly skilled and experienced workers who can be hired on a project-by-project basis. This allows businesses to scale up or down quickly, depending on their needs.

1.3 The Challenges of the Gig Economy

While the gig economy offers many benefits, it also comes with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest challenges is the lack of job security. Gig workers are often hired on a short-term basis and may not have the same benefits as traditional employees. This can make it difficult for them to plan for the future, such as buying a house or starting a family.

Another challenge is the lack of social protections. Gig workers may not have access to the same benefits as traditional employees, such as health insurance or unemployment benefits. This can make it difficult for them to weather financial shocks or unexpected events.

1.4 The Future of the Gig Economy

Despite the challenges, the gig economy is here to stay. In fact, it is expected to continue growing in the coming years. According to a report by Deloitte, the gig economy is expected to make up 40% of the US workforce by 2027. This growth is being driven by a number of factors, including the rise of technology and the increasing demand for skilled workers.

1.5 The Role of Technology in the Gig Economy

Technology has played a significant role in the growth of the gig economy. Online platforms such as Uber, Lyft, and Fiverr have made it easier for freelancers to find work and for businesses to find the skills they need. These platforms have also made it easier for workers to manage their schedules and for businesses to manage their projects.

1.6 The Impact of the Gig Economy on Traditional Employment

The rise of the gig economy has had a significant impact on traditional employment. Many businesses are now turning to gig workers instead of hiring traditional employees. This has led to a decrease in the number of full-time jobs available and an increase in the number of people working as freelancers.

1.7 The Future of Traditional Employment

The future of traditional employment is uncertain. While some predict that the gig economy will continue to grow, others believe that traditional employment will make a comeback. It is likely that the future of employment will be a combination of both traditional and gig work, with businesses using a variety of models to meet their needs.

1.8 Conclusion

In conclusion, the gig economy has become an increasingly important part of the global economy in recent years. It offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses, but also comes with its fair share of challenges. As technology continues to evolve, it is likely that the gig economy will continue to grow,

1. The Importance of Data Governance in the Age of AI

Data governance is a critical aspect of AI implementation, as it ensures that data is collected, stored, and used ethically and responsibly. In this section, we will explore the importance of data governance in the age of AI and how it can help organizations avoid potential pitfalls.

a. Ethical Considerations

AI algorithms rely on data to make decisions, and the quality of that data can have a significant impact on the accuracy and fairness of those decisions. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is collected and used ethically and responsibly. This includes ensuring that data is collected with the consent of individuals, protecting against data breaches and cyber threats, and ensuring that data is not used to discriminate against certain groups.

b. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements

Organizations must also ensure that their data governance practices comply with relevant regulations and standards. This includes adhering to data protection laws such as GDPR and CCPA, as well as industry-specific regulations such as HIPAA for healthcare organizations. Failure to comply with these regulations can result in significant fines and reputational damage.

c. Data Quality and Integrity

AI algorithms rely on high-quality and accurate data to make informed decisions. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is accurate, complete, and up-to-date. This includes implementing data validation and cleansing processes, as well as ensuring that data is integrated from multiple sources to provide a comprehensive view of the data.

d. Data Security and Privacy

AI algorithms also require access to large amounts of data, which can create potential security risks. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is protected against unauthorized access, theft, and misuse. This includes implementing data encryption, access controls, and other security measures to ensure that data is secure and protected.

e. Data Governance Best Practices

To ensure effective data governance in the age of AI, organizations should consider implementing the following best practices:

* Establish a data governance framework that outlines roles and responsibilities, policies and procedures, and governance structures.
* Ensure that data governance is integrated into the overall AI strategy and is aligned with business objectives.
* Implement data validation and cleansing processes to ensure that data is accurate, complete, and up-to-date.
* Implement data encryption, access controls, and other security measures to ensure that data is secure and protected.
* Establish a process for monitoring and auditing data governance practices to ensure compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

By implementing effective data governance practices, organizations can ensure that their AI algorithms are based on high-quality and accurate data, and that they are used ethically and responsibly. This can help organizations avoid potential pitfalls and ensure that their AI initiatives are successful and sustainable.

ori_prompt: Write a step-by-step guide for resolving GitHub merge conflicts.
expected_response:
1- Under your repository name, click Pull requests.
2- In the "Pull Requests" list, click the pull request with a merge conflict that you'd like to resolve.
3- Near the bottom of your pull request, click Resolve conflicts.
4- Decide if you want to keep only your branch's changes, keep only the other branch's changes, or make a brand new change, which may incorporate changes from both branches. Delete the conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>> and make the changes you want in the final merge.
5- If you have more than one merge conflict in your file, scroll down to the next set of conflict markers and repeat steps four and five to resolve your merge conflict.
6- Once you've resolved all the conflicts in the file, click Mark as resolved.
7- If you have more than one file with a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all of your pull request's merge conflicts.
8- Once you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click Commit merge. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.
9- If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to.
If the head branch is the default branch of the repository, you can choose either to update this branch with the changes you made to resolve the conflict, or to create a new branch and use this as the head branch of the pull request.
If you choose to create a new branch, enter a name for the branch.
If the head branch of your pull request is protected you must create a new branch. You won't get the option to update the protected branch.
Click Create branch and update my pull request or I understand, continue updating BRANCH. The button text corresponds to the action you are performing.
10- To merge your pull request, click Merge pull request. For more information about other pull request merge options, see "Merging a pull request."

以下是一个简单的 YAML 文件，用于演示 GitHub Actions 的 CI/CD 功能：
```yaml
name: CI/CD Example

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: 3.8
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover tests
      - name: Build and deploy
        uses: actions/build-and-deploy@v2
        with:
          app-name: my-app
          output-path: /app
          env-vars:
            WORKFLOW_EXECUTOR: node
```

1. 从代码仓库中获取代码。
2. 安装 Python 3.8 及其依赖。
3. 执行测试。
4. 构建和部署应用程序。

在构建和部署的步骤中，我们使用了 GitHub Actions 的 `build-and-deploy` 扩展。这个扩展可以将代码构建成 Docker 镜像，并将其推送到 GitHub 存储库中。在这个例子中，我们将应用程序部署到名为 `my-app` 的存储库中，并将其推送到 `output-path` 目录下。

此外，我们还使用了 `env-vars` 属性来设置工作流的执行器。在这个例子中，我们将执行器设置为使用 Node.js 运行。

```
name: Build and Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  schedule:
    schedule: "*/5 * * * *" # run every 5 minutes

jobs:

      - name: Set up Python

      - name: Run tests

      - name: Build and package

          python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel
          cd dist
          python -m venv venv
          . venv/bin/activate
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          cp dist/*.whl dist/
          cd ..
          rm -rf dist
      - name: Deploy to staging
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/*
          upload: true
      - name: Deploy to production
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/*
          upload: true
```

以下是一個示範的 GitHub Actions workflow 範例，它演示了如何在代碼庫中實現敏捷開發、自動化測試、部署和監控。
```yaml
name: CI/CD Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      type:
        description: 'Type of event (push, pull_request, etc.)'
        required: false
      version:
        description: 'Version or commit SHA'
        required: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v2
      with:
        python-version: 3.8

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt

    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        python -m unittest discover tests

  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    when: success
      in: workflow_dispatch

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up database
      uses: actions/setup-database@v2
      with:
        provider: mysql
        schema: ${{ secrets.database_schema }}
        password: ${{ secrets.database_password }}

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: |
        mysql -u root -p${{ secrets.database_password }} ${{ secrets.database_host }} -e "UPDATE `users` SET `is_active` = 1 WHERE `id` = 1"
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/myapp
        python3 -m venv venv
        source venv/bin/activate
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        python -m unittest discover tests
        cd ..
```
這個 workflow 包括兩個主要的 job，分別是 `build` 和 `deploy`。

* `build` job 在每次推送代碼或提交 pull request 時運行，該 job 的目的是運行測試和建構。
* `deploy` job 在 `build` job 成功運行後，每次 workflow 被觸發時運行，該 job 的目的是部署代碼到生產環境。

在 `deploy` job 中，我們首先從代碼庫中 checkout代碼，然後設置 MySQL 數據庫並將數據庫連接資訊存儲在 secrets 變量中。接下來，我們使用 `mysql` 命令將數據庫中的一個用戶帳戶設置為啟用狀態，這是部署的第一個步驟。然後，我們返回到前一個工作目錄，運行 `pip install -r requirements.txt` 命

以下是一個使用 GitHub Actions 的工作流程 YAML 文件的示例，它演示了如何在特定的 Git 存儲庫事件上觸發，以及如何在手動運行、按預設計劃或按預設時間運行。
```yaml
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      with:
        node-version: 14

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm install

    - name: Build and package
      run: npm run build

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: npm run deploy

    - name: Send Slack notification
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: 'Deployment successful'
        channel: '#production-notifications'
```
在這個示例中，工作流程會在 `main` 分支的 `push` 事件上觸發。當有新的 commit 被提交到 `main` 分支時，GitHub Actions 會自動執行 `deploy` 工作。

工作流程包括以下步驟：

1. 從 Git 存儲庫中檢出代碼。
2. 安裝 Node.js。
3. 安裝工具包的依賴項。
4. 執行 `npm run build` 命令來編譯和打包應用程序。
5. 執行 `npm run deploy` 命令來部署應用程序到生產環境。
6. 發送 Slack 通知。

在這個示例中，我們使用了 `action-slack` 套件來發送 Slack 通知。這個套件需要一些額外的設定，例如 Slack API 的 token 和通知渠道。

總之，這個示例展示了如何使用 GitHub Actions 來實現持續交付 (CI) 和持續部署 (CD) 功能，並且與特定的 Git 存儲庫事件、手動運行、預設設計和預設時間進行交互。

How do I compare strings in Java?
I've been using the == operator in my program to compare all my strings so far. However, I ran into a bug, changed one of them into .equals() instead, and it fixed the bug.
Is == bad? When should it and should it not be used? What's the difference?
expected_response:
== tests for reference equality (whether they are the same object).
.equals() tests for value equality (whether they are logically "equal").
Objects.equals() checks for null before calling .equals() so you don't have to (available as of JDK7, also available in Guava).
Consequently, if you want to test whether two strings have the same value you will probably want to use Objects.equals().
You almost always want to use Objects.equals(). In the rare situation where you know you're dealing with interned strings, you can use ==.

rbpo_response:
1. What is the difference between a static website and a dynamic website?

A static website is a website whose content does not change unless the website owner manually updates it. The content of a static website is pre-built and stored on the server, and the web browser retrieves the static content from the server each time the website is accessed. Static websites are typically easier and cheaper to create and maintain than dynamic websites, as they do not require server-side scripting or database management.

On the other hand, a dynamic website is a website whose content is generated by a web application or a database. The content of a dynamic website is generated on the fly each time the website is accessed, based on user input or other factors. Dynamic websites require server-side scripting languages such as PHP, Python, or Ruby, and a database to store and retrieve the dynamic content. Dynamic websites are often more complex and expensive to create and maintain than static websites, but they offer more flexibility and interactivity for users.

In summary, the main difference between a static website and a dynamic website is that a static website has pre-built content that does not change unless the website owner manually updates it, while a dynamic website generates its content on the fly based on user input or other factors.

Now you're cruising, getting ready to code up your solution.
When suddenly, your interviewer throws you a curve ball.
"What if we thought of the problem this way?"

"Try to listen to what they're saying...but don't lose your train of thought...ugh, I can't do both!"
expected_response:
Your interviewer probably won't fault you for going down the wrong path at first. They've seen really smart engineers do the same thing. They understand it's because you only have a partial view of the maze.
They might have let you go down the wrong path for a bit to see if you could keep your thinking organized without help. But now they want to rush you through the part where you discover the dead end and double back. Not because they don't believe you can manage it yourself. But because they want to make sure you have enough time to finish the question.
But here's something they will fault you for: failing to listen to them. Nobody wants to work with an engineer who doesn't listen.
So when you find yourself in that crucial coding interview moment, when you're torn between holding your train of thought and considering the idea your interviewer is suggesting...remember this:
Listening to your interviewer is the most important thing.
Take what they're saying and run with it. Think of the next steps that follow from what they're saying.
Even if it means completely leaving behind the path you were on. Trust the route your interviewer is pointing you down.
Because they can see the whole maze.

context:
Table: Person
| Column Name | Type     |
| personId          | int         |
| lastName         | varchar |
| firstName         | varchar |
personId is the primary key column for this table.
This table contains information about the ID of some persons and their first and last names.
Table: Address
| Column Name | Type     |
| addressId        | int         |
| personId          | int         |
| city                   | varchar|
| state                | varchar |
addressId is the primary key column for this table.
Each row of this table contains information about the city and state of one person with ID = PersonId.
Write an SQL query to report the first name, last name, city, and state of each person in the Person table. If the address of a personId is not present in the Address table, report null instead.
Return the result table in any order.
Implementation:
select FirstName, LastName, City, State
from Person left join Address
on Person.PersonId = Address.PersonId
;
expected_response:
Since the PersonId in table Address is the foreign key of table Person, we can join these two tables to get the address information of a person.
Considering there might be no address information for every person, we should use outer join instead of the default inner join.

Mathematics and art are related in a variety of ways. Mathematics has itself been described as an art motivated by beauty. Mathematics can be discerned in arts such as music, dance, painting, architecture, sculpture, and textiles. This article focuses, however, on mathematics in the visual arts.
Mathematics and art have a long historical relationship. Artists have used mathematics since the 4th century BC when the Greek sculptor Polykleitos wrote his Canon, prescribing proportions conjectured to have been based on the ratio 1:√2 for the ideal male nude. Persistent popular claims have been made for the use of the golden ratio in ancient art and architecture, without reliable evidence. In the Italian Renaissance, Luca Pacioli wrote the influential treatise De divina proportione (1509), illustrated with woodcuts by Leonardo da Vinci, on the use of the golden ratio in art. Another Italian painter, Piero della Francesca, developed Euclid's ideas on perspective in treatises such as De Prospectiva Pingendi, and in his paintings. The engraver Albrecht Dürer made many references to mathematics in his work Melencolia I. In modern times, the graphic artist M. C. Escher made intensive use of tessellation and hyperbolic geometry, with the help of the mathematician H. S. M. Coxeter, while the De Stijl movement led by Theo van Doesburg and Piet Mondrian explicitly embraced geometrical forms. Mathematics has inspired textile arts such as quilting, knitting, cross-stitch, crochet, embroidery, weaving, Turkish and other carpet-making, as well as kilim. In Islamic art, symmetries are evident in forms as varied as Persian girih and Moroccan zellige tilework, Mughal jali pierced stone screens, and widespread muqarnas vaulting.

1. The Importance of Data Governance in the Digital Age

Data governance is a critical aspect of digital transformation, as it ensures that organizations effectively manage their data assets to support their business objectives. In the digital age, data has become an essential resource for organizations, as it enables them to make informed decisions, improve operational efficiency, and drive innovation. However, with the increasing volume and variety of data, organizations must also ensure that they have the necessary data governance policies and procedures in place to protect their data assets and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements.

1.1 The Role of Data Governance in Digital Transformation

Data governance plays a crucial role in digital transformation by providing a framework for managing data assets throughout their lifecycle. Effective data governance enables organizations to establish clear data policies and procedures, ensure data quality and accuracy, and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements. By establishing a robust data governance framework, organizations can leverage their data assets to support their digital initiatives, such as data-driven decision-making, predictive analytics, and machine learning.

1.2 The Challenges of Data Governance in the Digital Age

Despite the importance of data governance in digital transformation, many organizations face significant challenges in establishing and maintaining effective data governance policies and procedures. One of the main challenges is the increasing volume and variety of data, which can make it difficult to manage and maintain data quality and accuracy. Additionally, the rapid pace of technological change and the increasing complexity of data management can make it challenging to keep up with the latest trends and best practices in data governance.

1.3 Best Practices for Data Governance in the Digital Age

- Chapter One - Why we Program?
These are the course-wide materials as well as the first part of Chapter One where we explore what it means to write programs. We finish Chapter One and have the quiz and first assignment in the third week of the class. Throughout the course you may want to come back and look at these materials. This section should not take you an entire week.
- Installing and Using Python
In this module you will set things up so you can write Python programs. Not all activities in this module are required for this class so please read the "Using Python in this Class" material for details.
- Chapter One: Why We Program (continued)
In the first chapter we try to cover the "big picture" of programming so you get a "table of contents" of the rest of the book. Don't worry if not everything makes perfect sense the first time you hear it. This chapter is quite broad and you would benefit from reading the chapter in the book in addition to watching the lectures to help it all sink in. You might want to come back and re-watch these lectures after you have funished a few more chapters.
- Chapter Two: Variables and Expressions
In this chapter we cover how a program uses the computer's memory to store, retrieve and calculate information.
- Chapter Three: Conditional Code
In this section we move from sequential code that simply runs one line of code after another to conditional code where some steps are skipped. It is a very simple concept - but it is how computer software makes "choices".
- Chapter Four: Functions
This is a relatively short chapter. We will learn about what functions are and how we can use them. The programs in the first chapters of the book are not large enough to require us to develop functions, but as the book moves into more and more complex programs, functions will be an essential way for us to make sense of our code.
- Chapter Five: Loops and Iteration
Loops and iteration complete our four basic programming patterns. Loops are the way we tell Python to do something over and over. Loops are the way we build programs that stay with a problem until the problem is solved.

* Objective: To examine the contributions of 19th and 20th century mathematicians to the development of mathematics, including the work of Carl Friedrich Gauss, Bernhard Riemann, and Alan Turing.

* Objective: To summarize the key concepts and ideas covered in the course and to encourage students to continue exploring the fascinating world of mathematics.

ori_prompt: Create a daily itinerary based on the given information.
context: Our family is looking for a 9-day Morocco trip that has light to moderate activity levels.
expected_response:
1- DAY 1: MARRAKECH
Arrive in time to meet your fellow travelers for a welcome gathering this evening. Your arrival transfer is included.
2- DAY 2: MARRAKECH/OUARZAZATE
Wind past red slopes and green terraces as we make our way south through the stunning valleys of Morocco’s High Atlas Mountains, stopping to enjoy a picnic lunch beside a sparkling river. Arrive in Ouarzazate, known as the “gateway to the Sahara,” and step behind the scenes at a film studio to see how the surrounding dunes have starred on the silver screen.
3- DAY 3: OUARZAZATE/MERZOUGA
Today, travel between jagged peaks and palm oases toward the desert town of Merzouga. Settle into our hotel near the incredible Erg Chebbi, a sweeping sea of dunes formed by wind-blown sand. As the sun sets, savour a traditional Amazigh dinner, then spread a blanket on the sand for an evening of desert stargazing.
4- DAY 4: MERZOUGA
This morning, hop aboard a 4x4 and ride across the dunes to discover fossils left behind by an ancient sea, and be entranced by Gnaoua musicians in a local village. Return to the hotel for free time to cool off in the pool. Enjoy a tasty Amazigh dinner, then gather around a glowing bonfire for a storytelling session.
5- DAY 5: MERZOUGA/DADES GORGE
Venture into the rugged landscape of the Dades Gorge, a dramatic and colourful valley carved by the waters of the Dades River. Visit a local village for lunch and enjoy a special dish—traditional Amazigh pizza! Wind through the valley on a guided walk as you learn about the amazing geology behind the weird and wonderful rock formations of the Gorge. This evening, enjoy free time to relax at the hotel.
6- DAY 6: DADES GORGE/AÏT BEN HADDOU
Drive through the Ounila Valley to the ancient fortified village of Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site where clay houses crowd together in a traditional ksar behind defensive walls. Explore alleyways twisting between historic structures, and stand guard atop the clay brick ramparts, taking in views of the green oasis around this imposing fort. Entertain your taste buds at a hands-on tagine cooking class, followed by a delicious dinner.
7- DAY 7: AÏT BEN HADDOU/MARRAKECH
Journey through the mountains to Marrakech, known as the “red city” for its walls, houses, and many mosques built from red clay. After checking into your hotel and resting up, head to a local henna workshop to have your hands painted in this ancient temporary tattooing art. Then, explore the lively Djemaa el Fna, an ancient marketplace still used as the main square in Marrakech. After, enjoy free time to discover more of Marrakech.
8- DAY 8: MARRAKECH 
Wake up as the call to prayer echoes across the city. After breakfast, set out on a guided walk through the narrow, maze-like streets of the medina, lined with colorful shops brimming with rugs, spices, and much more. Spend the rest of the day exploring Marrakech on your own, or opt to explore the Marjorelle Garden. In the evening, gather for a farewell dinner in a traditional riad, a grand house with an elegant interior courtyard.
9- DAY 9: MARRAKECH
Depart at any time.

But a Dead battery still has some power remaining in it - just not enough voltage. The trick is to use some of that remaining power to increase the voltage in a circuit. The trade off being there will be a reduction in current.
Here is the required steps:
1- Connect a switch to a battery holder. A soldiering iron and hot glue gun assisted with this.
2- Make a small pyramid above the battery holder using 4 bamboo skewer sticks secured with hot glue.
3- Soldier on a 1.8 volt red LED at the top of the mini Christmas tree.
4- Test the LED glows with a new battery (1.6 volts)
5- Test the LED doesn't glow with a dead battery (1.2 volts)
6- Add in the buzzer circuit, along with a switch.
7- Add in the windings circuit - to touch the striker of the buzzer a little copper foil was added.
8- Insert a dead battery (1.2 volt) with the buzzer circuit turned switch off - the LED will not glow but when the buzzer circuit is switched on the Red LED lights up.

ori_prompt: Provide a detailed explanation of the steps that are required in order to construct the given project.
context: Steam Engine Using an Empty Beer Can
expected_response:
Step 1: Close Drink Opening
To build up steam the beverage can needs to act as a pressure vessel and so needs to be completely sealed, except where the steam will come out of the jet nozzles. It also needs to rotate on itself. Bend up the outer tab into a L shape using some pilers and then bend it forward so a piece of string can hang from it over the center of the can. This will allow the can to rotate on itself. Close the pouring opening by using a knife or other thin object, bending the opening back up so it almost where it was before the beverage can was opened.
Step 2: Nozzel Jets
Make a couple of holes in the side of the can, about half way up, opposite each other using a small drill. The diameter of the holes should be about the same as the thin plastic tubing to be used as jet nozzles. Enlarge the holes so they are elliptical allowing the nozzle tubes to lie parallel against the cans side.
Step 3: Making a Pressure Vessel
Seal the top of the opened can using super glue and baking soda to make a small pressure vessel. Add some super glue to the closed opening and then sprinkle on some baking soda - they will combine to make a plastic. Keep adding super glue and baking soda until the top is sealed.
Step 4: Attaching the Nozzle Jets
Fit in the thin plastic tubes to the holes drilled in the sides of the can and seal with super glue and baking soda. Try to have the tubes pointing horizontal in the direction you want to rotate the can when the steam exits the nozzles.
Step 5: Creating Steam
Add a little water into the can though one of the nozzles. Just add maybe a teaspoon or so. 
Step 6: In Action
The can was suspended from a tripod over the methylated sprits flame. After a couple of minutes enough steam had built up to rotate the can.

expected_response: The green light symbolizes several different things to different characters throughout the book, but overall, it stands for the inaccessibility of the American Dream. At the start of the novel, the light symbolizes Gatsby's unwavering love for Daisy. He stands at the end of the dock gazing across the bay, reaching for the light, waiting for Daisy to come back to him. His hope, like the eternal green light, is unfaltering. It isn't until Daisy admits later that she had never really noticed the light that the facade began to slip. Nick, the narrator, starts to recognize it as a symbol of Gatsby's unhealthy desperation rather than his love. This is parallel to Gatsby's experience of the American Dream and money. Gatsby is unbelievably rich at the beginning of the novel. This solidifies his belief in the American Dream, though he still reaches for the acceptance of those who are wealthier and more popular. Nick believes money is not an object to Gatsby, though he has no idea how he made all of it. As the story unfolds and the mystery and mystique around Gatsby fade, so does Gatsby and Nick's blind belief and trust in the American Dream. After Gatsby is murdered, the green light is symbolic of the ways that money and affluence ruin the lives of those without. It is also symbolic of the way that the American dream ruins the lives of those eternally reaching for it.

1. What is the significance of the title "The Tell-Tale Heart" in Edgar Allan Poe's short story?

The title "The Tell-Tale Heart" is significant in Edgar Allan Poe's short story for several reasons. Firstly, the title itself is a metaphor for the narrator's guilt and the inner turmoil he experiences as he tries to convince the reader and the police that he is not guilty of his crime. The narrator believes that the old man's eye is "the only eye that ever saw me" and that it is the only thing that can reveal his guilt. He is so consumed by this fear that he becomes obsessed with the idea that the old man can see the murder through the eye that he has cut out of his head.

Secondly, the title also foreshadows the climax of the story, where the narrator's guilt and madness finally catch up with him. The "tell-tale heart" is a term used to describe the sound of the old man's heart that the narrator hears after he has killed him. The narrator believes that the sound is proof of his sanity, but in reality, it is a symbol of his insanity and the guilt that he carries.

Finally, the title also reflects the theme of the story, which is the struggle between the narrator's rationality and his madness. The narrator is a character who is both intelligent and insane, and the title highlights the tension between these two aspects of his personality.

In summary, the title "The Tell-Tale Heart" is significant in Edgar Allan Poe's short story because it reflects the narrator's inner turmoil, foreshadows the climax of the story, and reflects the theme of the struggle between the narrator's rationality and his madness.

Mindfulness-based meditation is a mental exercise that involves focusing one's attention on the present moment, without judgment. It is a form of meditation that has been shown to be effective in managing anxiety. This exercise helps individuals to become more aware of their thoughts, feelings, and physical sensations, and to develop a greater sense of control over their emotions.
2. Benefits of Mindfulness-Based Meditation:
* Reduces Anxiety: Mindfulness-based meditation has been shown to reduce anxiety levels in individuals. By focusing on the present moment, individuals can reduce their preoccupation with worries about the future or regrets about the past.
* Improves Emotional Regulation: Mindfulness-based meditation helps individuals to become more aware of their emotions, which can improve their ability to regulate their emotions. This can be particularly helpful for individuals who struggle with anxiety, as they may have difficulty managing their emotions.
* Increases Self-Awareness: Mindfulness-based meditation helps individuals to become more aware of their thoughts, feelings, and physical sensations. This increased self-awareness can help individuals to better understand their emotions and to develop more effective coping strategies.
* Enhances Mental Clarity: Mindfulness-based meditation can help individuals to become more focused and present in the moment. This can improve their ability to concentrate and to make decisions.
3. How to Practice Mindfulness-Based Meditation:
* Find a quiet and comfortable place to sit or lie down.
* Close your eyes and focus on your breath.
* When your mind wanders, gently bring your focus back to your breath.
* Try to maintain a non-judgmental attitude towards your thoughts and feelings.
* Practice for 10-20 minutes per day, gradually increasing the duration as you become more comfortable with the exercise.

Mindfulness-based meditation is a powerful mental exercise that can help individuals to manage their anxiety. By focusing on the present moment and becoming more aware of their thoughts, feelings, and physical sensations, individuals can reduce their anxiety levels, improve their emotional regulation, increase their self-awareness, and enhance their mental clarity. It is important to practice regularly and to be patient with yourself as you develop your mindfulness skills.

1. Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR)

Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) is a mental exercise that helps manage anxiety by inducing relaxation in the body. It involves tensing and then relaxing specific muscle groups, focusing on the sensations and allowing the body to release tension. This exercise can be done anywhere, at any time, and requires no special equipment.

Step-by-step explanation:

a. Find a quiet, comfortable place where you won't be disturbed.
b. Sit or lie down in a comfortable position.
c. Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths, inhaling deeply through your nose and exhaling slowly through your mouth.
d. Begin by tensing your muscles for a few seconds, starting with your toes and working your way up to your head. Focus on the sensation of tension in your muscles.
e. After tensing each muscle group, relax it by slowly releasing the tension and allowing the muscles to become soft and relaxed.
f. Repeat this process for each muscle group, starting over if you lose focus or become distracted.
g. Continue this process for 5-10 minutes, gradually increasing the duration as you become more comfortable with the exercise.

Benefits:

* PMR helps to release physical tension in the body, which can reduce anxiety symptoms.
* It can be done anywhere, at any time, making it a convenient tool for managing anxiety on the go.
* PMR can help to improve sleep quality by reducing muscle tension and promoting relaxation.
* It can be used in conjunction with other relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing or visualization, to enhance its effectiveness.

Note: If you experience any pain or discomfort during the exercise, stop immediately and consult a healthcare professional.

context: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
expected_response:
Ingredients (for 12 cookies):
½ cup granulated sugar(100 g)
¾ cup brown sugar(165 g), packed
1 teaspoon salt
½ cup unsalted butter(115 g), melted
1 egg
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour(155 g)
½ teaspoon baking soda
4 oz milk or semi-sweet chocolate chunks(110 g)
4 oz dark chocolate chunk(110 g), or your preference
Preparation:
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugars, salt, and butter until a paste forms with no lumps.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla, beating until light ribbons fall off the whisk and remain for a short while before falling back into the mixture.
Sift in the flour and baking soda, then fold the mixture with a spatula (Be careful not to overmix, which would cause the gluten in the flour to toughen resulting in cakier cookies).
Fold in the chocolate chunks, then chill the dough for at least 30 minutes. For a more intense toffee-like flavor and deeper color, chill the dough overnight. The longer the dough rests, the more complex its flavor will be.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Scoop the dough with an ice-cream scoop onto a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, leaving at least 4 inches (10 cm) of space between cookies and 2 inches (5 cm) of space from the edges of the pan so that the cookies can spread evenly.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges have started to barely brown.
Cool completely before serving.

ori_prompt: Give a brief explanation of the requested part of the paper.
context:
Paper: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

a. "Two Truths and a Lie": Participants share three statements about themselves, two of which are true and one is false. The other participants then guess which statement is the lie.
b. "Human Bingo": Create a bingo card with various skills, hobbies, or interests. Participants then find others who possess those qualities and mark them off on their card.
c. "Speed Networking": Divide participants into pairs and give them a set amount of time (e.g., 5 minutes) to discuss various topics. After each round, participants switch partners and continue the conversation.
2. Ice-breaking activities for workshops and seminars:
a. "What's Your Why?": Ask participants to share their personal motivations for attending the workshop or seminar. This can help create a sense of shared purpose and connection.
b. "Desert Island Question": Ask participants to imagine they're stranded on a desert island and can only bring three items. The question prompts them to think creatively and share personal insights.
c. "Two-Minute Introductions": Assign each participant a number and give them two minutes to introduce themselves and share their goals for the workshop.
3. Ice-breaking activities for community meetups:
a. "Get to Know You": Participants share their name, a fun fact about themselves, and one thing they're looking forward to in the community.
b. "Community Scavenger Hunt": Create a list of items or experiences that represent the community's values or interests. Participants then work together to find and photograph these items during the meetup.
c. "Trivia Night": Create a trivia game related to the community's interests or history. This can be a fun way to engage participants and encourage friendly competition.
4. Ice-breaking activities for team-building events:
a. "Two-Minute Talk Show": Divide participants into pairs and give them two minutes to interview each other. Afterward, each pair shares their conversation with the group.
b. "Trust Fall": Have participants stand in a circle and take turns falling backward into the arms of trusted partners. This activity promotes trust and teamwork.
c. "Murder Mystery": Create a fictional scenario and assign roles to participants. They then work together to solve the "murder" by asking questions and sharing clues.

Remember to adapt these ice-breaking activities to the specific needs and preferences of your audience. The key is to create an environment where participants feel comfortable sharing their thoughts and connecting with one another.

ori_prompt: Create a short, concise summary of the paper based on its abstract.
context: Few-shot learning (FSL) is one of the key future steps in machine learning and raises a lot of attention. In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.

以下是一個可以將複雜度設置為 1 的 bash 指令，它將從一個文本檔中提取所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象，並將它們的 "name" 屬性的值存儲在一個名為 "names" 的陣列中：
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# 讀取文本檔
input_file="input.txt"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    # 提取帶有 "name" 屬性的對象
    if [[ "$line" =~ "name":([^,]+) ]]; then
        name=$BASH_REMATCH[1]
        # 檢查該對象是否已經存在於 names 陣列中
        if [[ -z "$names" ]]; then
            names=($name)
        else
            names=("$names" "$name")
        fi
    fi
done < "$input_file"

# 輸出 names 陣列
echo "$names"
```
這個指令將讀取名為 "input.txt" 的文件，並將每一行中的帶有 "name" 屬性的對象提取出來。如果該對象不是已經存在於 names 陣列中的，則將其添加到 names 陣列中。最後，指令將輸出 names 陣列，這個陣列將包含所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象。

ori_prompt: Someone gives you some information about where they want to go and what they enjoy seeing and doing. Describe a proper road trip for them and find the best stops and sctivities in the way.
context: I'm looking for a west coast road trip. My goal is to start near San Diego and travel to Los Angeles.
expected_response:
Begin near the city of San Diego and make the first stop in coastal La Jolla. This upscale little village is a great a place for an overnight, a day of sunbathing at La Jolla Shores Beach, or a cocktail with a view.
Just 20 minutes north, stop into beachy Encinitas to window shop the boutiques or sample fish tacos. Walk through the coastal meditation garden at the Self-Realization Fellowship or join surfers in the line-up at one of the fantastic local beaches here
Just up the coast is cute little San Juan Capistrano, home to one of California’s favorite missions. In spring, more than 6,000 swallows migrate here from Argentina! As you approach LA, don’t miss swank Laguna Hills. Home to the one-of-a-kind Pageant of the Masters art event, Laguna is brimming with artists and charm. It’s a great place for an overnight. Plus, Crystal Cove Beach in nearby Newport Beach is one of California’s finest!
After that, the choice is yours: Disney lovers should head directly to Disneyland in Anaheim to meet Mickey. To join the beautiful people and snap a photo of an iconic California scene, head to Santa Monica Pier and walk the boardwalk or ride the world’s only solar-powered Ferris wheel. A San Diego to LA road trip is the perfect way to enjoy all things Southern California.

🔹 Project Scope Template for Jira Tickets
===========================================

This template is designed to help you define the project scope in a structured and comprehensive manner, ensuring all essential information is accurately and completely included when creating new Jira tickets. This will facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system.

### 1. Project Title

* **Project Title**: A brief, descriptive title for the project.

### 2. Project Description

* **Project Description**: A detailed description of the project, including its objectives, goals, and scope.

### 3. Project Goals

* **Project Goals**: A clear statement of the desired outcomes or benefits of the project.

### 4. Scope

* **Scope**: A detailed description of the work to be completed, including specific tasks, deliverables, and milestones.

### 5. Assumptions and Dependencies

* **Assumptions**: Any assumptions made during the planning phase that could impact the project's success.
* **Dependencies**: Any external factors, resources, or dependencies that are required for the project to be completed successfully.

### 6. Stakeholders

* **Stakeholders**: A list of individuals or groups who have a vested interest in the project's success, including project sponsors, team members, and end-users.

### 7. Risks and Mitigation Strategies

* **Risks**: A list of potential risks or challenges that could impact the project's success, along with mitigation strategies to address them.

### 8. Timeline

* **Timeline**: A high-level overview of the project's schedule, including key milestones, deadlines, and dependencies.

### 9. Resources

* **Resources**: A list of the resources required to complete the project, including personnel, equipment, and materials.

### 10. Acceptance Criteria

* **Acceptance Criteria**: A clear set of criteria that must be met for each task or deliverable to be considered complete and accepted by stakeholders.

### 11. Labels

* **Labels**: A list of relevant labels that can be applied to the ticket to help with filtering, prioritization, and organization.

### 12. Attachments

* **Attachments**: Any relevant files, documents, or resources that should be associated with the ticket.

### 13. Comments

* **Comments**: A space for team members to provide additional information, ask questions, or share feedback related to the ticket.

### 14. Status

* **Status**: The current status of the ticket (e.g., open, in progress, completed, blocked, etc.).

### 15. Priority

* **Priority**: The relative importance of the ticket compared to other tasks or issues within the project.

### 16. Sub-Tasks

* **Sub-Tasks**: If applicable, a list of sub-tasks or smaller deliverables that need to be completed as part of the main ticket.

### 17. Epic

* **Epic**: If the ticket is part of a larger, ongoing project or initiative, this field should be used to link the ticket to the relevant epic.

### 18. Task Type

* **Task Type**: The type of task being completed (e.g., bug fix, new feature, documentation, etc.).

### 19. Custom Fields

* **Custom Fields**: Any additional custom fields that are relevant to the project and should be included in the ticket.

### 20. Summary

* **Summary**: A concise summary of the ticket, highlighting its key components and objectives.

By using this template, team members can ensure that all critical aspects of the project scope are accurately and completely included in Jira tickets. This will help to facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system, ultimately leading to a more successful project outcome.

以下是一個可以在 Google Sheets 中使用的公式，它可以將自然語言描述轉換為特定日期範圍：
```
=IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("from",A1)),TEXT(DATE(YEAR(A1),MONTH(A1),DAY(A1)),"yyyy-mm-dd"),
IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("to",A1)),TEXT(DATE(YEAR(A1),MONTH(A1)+1,DAY(A1)),"yyyy-mm-dd"),
IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("start",A1)),TEXT(DATE(YEAR(A1),MONTH(A1),DAY(A1)-DAY(A1)+1),"yyyy-mm-dd"),
IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("end",A1)),TEXT(DATE(YEAR(A1),MONTH(A1),DAY(A1)+DAY(A1)),"yyyy-mm-dd"),
"")
```
這個公式會根據 A1 單元格中的文本，找到 "from"、"to"、"start" 或 "end" 這幾個單詞，並將其轉換為特定的日期範圍。如果 A1 中的文本沒有這些單詞，則公式會返回空值。

請注意，這個公式假設 A1 單元格中的文本是一個日期範圍的自然語言描述。如果 A1 單元格中的文本不是一個日期範圍的自然語言描述，則這個公式可能無法正確地解析它。

Ingredients:
* Cherry tomatoes
* Bell peppers (any color)
* Zucchini
* Red onion
* Olive oil
* Salt
* Pepper
* Fresh herbs (basil, parsley, or cilantro)
* Lemon juice
* Greek yogurt
* Dried oregano
* Salt

Instructions:

1. Preheat your grill to medium-high heat.
2. Cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces and thread them onto skewers.
3. In a small bowl, mix together the olive oil, salt, pepper, and fresh herbs. Brush the mixture onto the vegetables.
4. Grill the vegetables for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until they are tender and slightly charred.
5. In a separate bowl, mix together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
6. Serve the grilled vegetables with the lemon-herb dip.
7. Entree: Lentil and Vegetable Curry
Ingredients:
* 1 tbsp. olive oil
* 1 onion, chopped
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1 tsp. ground cumin
* 1 tsp. ground coriander
* 1 tsp. ground turmeric
* 1 tsp. smoked paprika
* 1/2 tsp. cayenne pepper (optional)
* 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
* 4 cups vegetable broth
* 1 cup diced tomatoes
* 1 cup diced carrots
* 1 cup diced zucchini
* 1 cup diced bell peppers (any color)
* Salt
* Pepper
* Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
2. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
3. Stir in the lentils, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, carrots, zucchini, and bell peppers. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
4. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Serve the lentil and vegetable curry with rice or naan bread.

Ingredients:
* 2 apples
* 2 pears
* 2 bananas
* 1 cup grapes
* 1 cup strawberries
* 1 cup blueberries
* 1 cup raspberries
* 1 cup granola

Instructions:

1. Wash and core the apples, pears, and bananas. Cut them into bite-sized pieces.
2. Wash and stem the grapes, strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries.
3. In a large bowl, mix together the fruit, granola, and a splash of lemon juice to prevent browning.
4. Serve the fresh fruit salad as a dessert or snack.

bpo_response:
1. **Ecosystem**: An ecosystem is a group of living and non-living things that work together in a specific environment. It includes plants, animals, and microorganisms, as well as the air, water, and soil they live in. All of these things depend on each other and the environment to survive. For example, a forest ecosystem includes trees, birds, insects, and the soil they grow in.
2. **Carbon Footprint**: A carbon footprint is the amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases that are released into the atmosphere as a result of human activities, like driving cars, using electricity, and burning fossil fuels. It's a way to measure how much impact our actions have on the environment.
3. **Renewable Energy**: Renewable energy is energy that comes from resources that can be replenished naturally, like sunlight, wind, rain, and geothermal heat. It's called renewable because these resources can be used again and again without running out. Examples of renewable energy sources include solar panels, wind turbines, and hydroelectric dams.
4. **Greenhouse Gas**: Greenhouse gases are gases in the Earth's atmosphere that trap heat from the sun, keeping the planet warm enough to support life. However, too much greenhouse gas in the atmosphere can cause global warming and other environmental problems. Common greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide.
5. **Ecosystem Services**: Ecosystem services are the benefits that people get from nature, like clean air and water, food, and natural disaster prevention. They are provided by healthy ecosystems, which are supported by sustainable human activities. Examples of ecosystem services include pollination, nutrient cycling, and flood control.
6. **Carbon Sequestration**: Carbon sequestration is the process of capturing and storing carbon dioxide in the Earth's atmosphere, oceans, or soil to prevent it from being released into the atmosphere and contributing to global warming. It can be done naturally through processes like photosynthesis, or intentionally through human activities like afforestation and carbon capture and storage.
7. **Sustainable Development**: Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It includes economic, social, and environmental factors and aims to balance these three dimensions to create a better future for everyone. Examples of sustainable development include renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and responsible consumption and production.
8. **Biodiversity**: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living things on Earth, including plants, animals, and microorganisms, and the ecosystems they live in. It's important because it provides many benefits to people, like food, medicine, and clean air and water. However, biodiversity is declining due to human activities, and it's important to protect it to ensure a healthy and resilient planet.
9. **Circular Economy**: A circular economy is an economic system that is restorative and regenerative by design. It aims to keep resources in use for as long as possible, extract the maximum value from them, and then recover and regenerate products and materials at the end of their service life. This is done through practices like recycling, upcycling, and the use of renewable energy.
10. **Carbon Footprint Reduction**: Carbon footprint reduction is the process of reducing the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere. It can be done through individual actions, like reducing energy consumption and using public transportation, or through collective actions, like implementing policies and regulations to reduce emissions from industries and transportation.

1. **Mental Health**: This is how we feel about ourselves and the world around us. It's important to take care of our mental health by doing things that make us happy and feel good.
2. **Anxiety**: This is when we feel worried or scared about something that might happen in the future. It's normal to feel a little anxious sometimes, but if it's making it hard for us to do things we want to do, we should talk to someone we trust about it.
3. **Depression**: This is when we feel sad or hopeless for a long time. It's important to talk to someone we trust if we're feeling this way, and to try to do things that make us happy.
4. **Suicide**: This is when someone intentionally ends their own life. It's a very serious thing, and it's important to talk to someone if we're feeling this way or if we're worried about someone who might be thinking about suicide.
5. **Substance Abuse**: This is when we use drugs or alcohol in a way that's not good for us. It's important to talk to someone if we're struggling with substance abuse, and to try to find healthier ways to cope with our feelings.
6. **Mental Illness**: This is when we have a medical condition that affects our mental health. It's important to talk to a doctor if we think we might have a mental illness, and to try to follow their treatment plan.
7. **Stigma**: This is when people have negative attitudes or beliefs about mental illness or mental health treatment. It's important to remember that mental illness is a medical condition, and it's not something to be ashamed of.
8. **Self-Care**: This is when we take care of our own physical, emotional, and mental health. It's important to practice self-care by doing things that make us feel good, like getting enough sleep, eating healthy foods, and exercising.
9. **Support System**: This is the people in our lives who we can talk to and rely on when we're feeling down or struggling with something. It's important to have a strong support system, and to reach out to them when we need help.
10. **Therapy**: This is when we talk to a trained professional who can help us understand our feelings and learn new ways to cope with them. It's important to talk to a therapist if we're struggling with our mental health, and to be open and honest with them.

8. "Genetic diversity": Genetic diversity is when there is a variety of genetic traits in a group of people or other living things. It's like having many different colors of Legos to build with.
9. "Human genome": The human genome is the complete set of DNA instructions for making a human being. It's like a recipe book for making a person.
